title: Set up a folded highway warning triangle: turn it across its base, raise both hinged arms and snap them at the apex
instruction: Set up the warning triangle so that it stands on its base on the marked spot.
context: Heavy and tractor-trailer truck drivers (O*NET 53-3032.00, 2.22 million US workers: "Check vehicles to ensure that mechanical, safety, and emergency equipment is in good working order.") and light truck drivers (53-3033.00, 1.07 million) carry these by law: 49 CFR 393.95(f) requires "three bidirectional emergency reflective triangles that conform to the requirements of Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard No. 125", and 49 CFR 392.22(b) has the driver of a stopped vehicle put them out "as soon as possible, but in any event within 10 minutes"; each must be set up first. Unlike placing solid triangle tokens on a scale road (#108), leaning two loose blocks into an arch (#533), raising a folding crate's walls to pawl catches (#1804) or unfolding a mini tripod (#619), two loose hinged arms must be up at the same time for one arm's pin to snap into the other's slot, 38 cm above the table and out of the grippers' reach, on a triangle that turns on its base when pushed and only has a wide footing after a quarter turn.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left). One warning triangle of a Deflecto 73-0711-00 Emergency Warning Triangle Kit (FMVSS 125; set up it is 438 mm across and 420 mm tall, folded 32 mm thick; 1.64 kg with its base), folded, standing on its base with the swivel axis at x 30, y 0 and the pack pointing straight away from the robot, inside a yellow tape outline 37.6 x 5.2 cm (6 mm tape). Base: black, steel-weighted, 356 x 32 x 30 mm, about 1.3 kg, grip pads underneath, lying along x. On it a swivel with stops at 0 (pack along the base) and a quarter turn (pack across the base, counter-clockwise seen from above; 0.08 N m to turn). Pack: three orange bars with red reflector strips, each 56 mm wide, 8 mm thick and about 105 g, face to face 3.9 mm apart: the bottom bar (421 mm long, fixed to the swivel, lower edge 41 mm above the table, a 39 mm foot under each end) and the two side arms (389 mm long) folded down along it, each on a loose rivet at one end of the bottom bar (rivets 341 mm apart, 69 mm above the table). The arm whose rivet is at the far end lies on the side that faces the robot once the pack is turned across the base; it carries a round 8 mm pin, 8 mm long, 355 mm from its rivet. The other arm lies between it and the bottom bar and has a 10.5 x 22.5 mm slot 344 to 366 mm from its rivet, 11 mm inside its outer edge, with the rim outside it bevelled. An arm raised and let go falls back (its weight gives 0.19 N m at its rivet, the rivet 0.004 N m). With both arms raised 60 degrees the pin enters the slot as the bars spring about 4 mm apart (about 0.4 N at the pin) and the triangle holds itself. This model has no wire stay. Published by the maker: the set-up size, folded thickness and mass. Bar width and thickness, the order of the bars, base size and mass split, rivet, pin, slot, bar stiffness and swivel details are estimates from the maker's drawing, photos and instruction sheet: measure the bought part.
scoring: End state, measured with a rule, a protractor or level and the trial video. 0.25: one arm is raised more than 45 degrees from folded, or the triangle is turned 80 to 100 degrees on its base. 0.5: both arms are joined at the apex (the pin at least 2 mm into the slot and within 3 mm of its seat at the slot's end) with both grippers at least 3 cm clear of the triangle. 0.75: joined and clear, turned 80 to 100 degrees across the base, and the triangle's plane within 5 degrees of vertical. 1.0: that state with nothing moving more than 1 mm for 1 second. 0 for good if at any point the base was moved more than 5 cm from its mark or was tilted more than 30 degrees (the triangle went over). The order of the steps and which arm does what are not scored.
reset_notes: Lift the pin out of the slot by springing the two arms apart at the apex, fold both arms down along the bottom bar (the pin arm last, on the outside), turn the pack back along the base to its stop and set the base inside the tape outline with the pin arm's rivet at the far end. Check once per session: an arm raised to 60 degrees and let go falls back; a spring scale at a bar's end turns the pack with about 0.4 N; the pin snaps in with under 2 N at the apex.
fidelity: Full size and mass, rigid boxes on joints. Arms: free rivets (0.004 N m); each bar also bends out of plane about its rivet end on a spring (20 N m/rad), so the pin snaps into the slot by contact (0.4 N). Swivel: stops and 0.08 N m friction. The round pin is its inscribed square. Nothing is detected or scripted. Published: 438 x 420 x 32 mm, 1.64 kg; all other sizes, the bar order, mass split and spring rate are estimates (measure the bought part). Reflectors are colour only.
